papers.title: Photochromic Bisphenoxyl Radical Complexes via Homolytic Spiro C–O Bond Cleavage
papers.authors: Daisuke Tanaka, Paulina H. Marek-Urban, Shunsuke Kobashi, Yoichi Kobayashi
papers.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.archiveJournal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.summary: UV-driven cleavage of a spiro C–O bond creates a bisphenoxyl radical pair whose recombination depends strongly on the molecular bridge. Time-resolved infrared spectroscopy supports biradical formation. The reported microsecond lifetime describes chemical persistence, rather than a measured spin-coherence time.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Light-controlled radical generation suggests molecular design ideas for switchable spin-bearing systems; qubit coherence remains untested.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine structural motifs that stabilize or generate multiple organic radical centers.

papers.title: Spin preservation in screw-symmetric molecules
papers.authors: Jonas Bloch, Fedor Baranov, Maxim Breitkreiz
papers.summary: Analytical and tight-binding models predict that discrete screw symmetry can protect spin during transport through long molecules. Protection weakens when the symmetry is broken. Simulated spin-valve magnetoresistance provides a proposed experimental signature, rather than a demonstration of molecular-qubit coherence.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Symmetry-dependent spin preservation connects to chiral molecular frameworks, although the observable here is transport spin fidelity.

relatedPapers.reason: Both connect molecular chirality and structure to spin behavior, using different physical mechanisms.

papers.title: A robust spin-coupled tetraradical via nonalternant design
papers.authors: Weixiang Zhou, Yu-Shuang Zhang, Gaetano Ricci, Yubin Fu, David Casanova, Juan Casado, Shang-Da Jiang, Junzhi Liu
papers.summary: A nonalternant tetraradical combines air stability with a strongly correlated singlet ground state and competing exchange interactions. Electronic-structure and magnetic analyses connect its fused-ring topology to spin robustness. The study reports reduced decoherence and long relaxation and coherence times without equating these with chemical stability.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Stable multiradical scaffolds are directly relevant to molecular spin architectures and exchange-coupling design.

relatedPapers.reason: Both develop organic multiradical structures and relate molecular topology to spin properties.

papers.title: RF-free control of nuclear spins with color centers in silicon carbide
papers.authors: Raphael Wörnle, Jonathan Körber, Timo Steidl, Georgy V. Astakhov, Durga B. R. Dasari, Florian Kaiser, Vadim Vorobyov, Jörg Wrachtrup
papers.summary: A modified silicon-carbide divacancy enables coherent manipulation of a coupled nuclear spin using electron-spin microwave pulses. A tilted magnetic field activates hyperfine-enhanced control, removing the additional RF drive. Experiments characterize two-qubit states and nuclear coherence approaching the relaxation limit.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Electron-mediated nuclear control offers a useful comparison for simplifying molecular electron–nuclear spin manipulation.

relatedPapers.reason: Both address coherent manipulation of localized spin qubits; the host and coupling mechanisms differ.

papers.title: Extension of coherence time beyond breakeven point using only drives and dissipation
papers.authors: Lida Sun, Yifang Xu, Yilong Zhou, Ziyue Hua, Weiting Wang, Jie Zhou, Zi-Jie Chen, Lui Zuccherelli de Paula, Qing-Xuan Jie, Guangming Xue, Haifeng Yu, Weizhou Cai, Chang-Ling Zou, Luyan Sun
papers.summary: An autonomous correction protocol transfers photon-loss error information to resettable ancillas using drives and dissipation. In a bosonic binomial code, the logical coherence time reaches 1.04 times that of the best physical qubit, demonstrating a modest experimental crossing of the breakeven point.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Engineered dissipation provides a complementary strategy to dynamical protection, with performance assessed against an explicit physical-qubit baseline.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate techniques for reducing decoherence-related errors, with different control and encoding strategies.

papers.title: Transient State Preservation of a Dissipative Qubit via Lyapunov Control
papers.summary: A Lindblad-model study derives Lyapunov feedback for transient qubit-state preservation. Simulations identify target-dependent benefits under amplitude damping and more limited gains under dephasing. Collinear Bloch vectors eliminate control authority, clarifying why the method cannot universally stabilize states or remove irreversible dissipation.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: The explicit limits of Hamiltonian feedback help distinguish finite-time state protection from universal decoherence suppression.

relatedPapers.reason: Both concern control strategies for protecting quantum information against environmental errors.

papers.title: Nuclear quadrupole resonance spectroscopy as an operando tool for mechanochemistry
papers.authors: César Leroy, Danielle Laurencin, Daniel Valenza, Patrice Montels, Philippe Gaveau
papers.summary: Operando nuclear quadrupole resonance follows ball-milling formation of a halogen-bonded cocrystal and a hybrid perovskite. The setup also tracks temperature inside the milling jar, providing a magnetic-resonance route to monitoring reaction evolution alongside existing mechanochemical characterization methods.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Real-time resonance measurements could inform the design of experiments connecting solid-state reaction kinetics and crystallization.

relatedPapers.reason: Both emphasize resolving synthesis kinetics to understand how crystalline materials form.

papers.title: Axis-selective AC magnetic-field imaging in the tens-of-megahertz regime using RF-dressed continuous-wave scanning NV magnetometry
papers.authors: Shuntaro Komuro, Ryusei Okaniwa, Kazuma Okura, Kunitaka Hayashi, Toshu An, Junko Ishi-Hayase
papers.summary: RF-dressed continuous-wave scanning NV magnetometry images an AC magnetic field at 33.5 MHz without synchronized high-power microwave pulses. Selecting three NV axes yields maps of field-projection magnitudes. Full vector reconstruction would require additional phase information beyond the demonstrated imaging measurements.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Continuous-wave imaging and explicit projection limits are pertinent to robust quantum-sensor readout and artifact interpretation.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine how sensing protocols shape reliable magnetic-field measurements.

papers.title: Physics-guided machine learning for sim-to-real calibration of NV diamond magnetometers
papers.authors: Jonathan Daniel, Sangwoo Lee, Jesse Hernandez, Emanuel Suarez, Jinhee Lee, Je-Hyung Kim, Martin Y. Kim
papers.summary: A physics-guided learning model embeds Zeeman splitting into NV-magnetometer calibration. Sparse experimental seeds anchor a larger synthetic dataset, improving scalar-field prediction relative to a statistical baseline and transferring to raw experimental spectra. The study targets practical calibration rather than vector-field reconstruction.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Physics-constrained calibration offers a complementary approach to reducing measurement bias in quantum sensing.

relatedPapers.reason: Both seek more reliable quantum-sensor outputs by addressing systematic measurement limitations.

papers.title: DFT-assisted natural abundance 13 C zero-field NMR via optical magnetometry
papers.authors: Blake Andrews, Xiao Liu, Raphael Zumbrunn, Calvin Lee, Sahand Adibnia, Emanuel Druga, Martin Head-Gordon, Ashok Ajoy
papers.summary: A compact rubidium magnetometer detects natural-abundance carbon-13 zero-field NMR spectra from ordinary liquids without hyperpolarization. Vibrationally corrected DFT helps interpret molecular fingerprints; remaining spectral discrepancies carry information about solution interactions, including hydrogen bonding and ion pairing.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Coupling spin-sensitive detection with chemical interpretation complements framework-based molecular and ionic recognition.

relatedPapers.reason: Both use spin-related observables for chemical identification, through distinct sensors and recognition mechanisms.

papers.title: A Thiazolo[5,4- d ]thiazole-Functionalized Metal–Organic Framework Enabling Dual-Mode Fluorescent/Electrochemical Hg 2+ Sensing and In Situ Imaging
papers.authors: Shihang Qin, Zihan Li, Haoyuan Jia, Junlei Sun, Zihan Feng, Shitong Yin, Yidan Xie, Pengyan Wu, Jian Wang
papers.summary: A thiazolothiazole-functionalized zinc MOF detects mercury ions through fluorescence and differential-pulse voltammetry. Coordination at nitrogen and sulfur sites links recognition to both signals. Spiked-water tests and simulated produce imaging demonstrate analytical applications without establishing clinical or unrestricted field performance.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Framework-integrated recognition sites and dual readouts provide useful comparisons for selective chemical sensing.

relatedPapers.reason: Both incorporate chemical recognition functionality into a porous framework for ion detection.

papers.title: Electronic Structure of Co-Phthalocyanine Metal–Organic Framework
papers.authors: Norihiro Morishita, Momoka Isobe, Kenichi Ozawa, Jun’ya Tsutsumi, Kaname Kanai
papers.summary: Calculations and spectroscopy examine why a cobalt-phthalocyanine MOF is semiconducting rather than metallic. Thin-flake optical measurements reveal a small gap, while DFT+U captures key electronic features. The analysis indicates that electron correlation is important and stacking alone does not explain the observed behavior.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Reconciling calculated bands with measured gaps is directly relevant to interpreting conductive-framework electronic structures.

relatedPapers.reason: Both connect framework electronic structure with experimentally observed band behavior.

papers.title: Amine Vapor Activated Superior Proton Conduction in a Barium Metal–Organic Framework
papers.authors: Rui-Lan Liu, Shuhui Zhao, Yueyun Yang, Jing Li, Dan-Yang Wang, Gang Li
papers.summary: Amine-vapor exposure strongly enhances proton conduction in a barium MOF under humid conditions. Ammonia treatment changes the available proton-transport environment and increases measured conductivity at elevated temperature. The reported response concerns ionic transport, rather than an established improvement in electronic conductivity.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Atmosphere-dependent proton transport highlights the need to distinguish ionic and electronic contributions in framework devices.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate changes in apparent transport behavior induced by the surrounding atmosphere.

papers.title: High-κ bismuth molybdate single-crystalline dielectric for high-temperature two-dimensional transistors
papers.authors: Yujing Qiao, Yue Tang, Yurong An, Lei Zhang, Yingying Li, Guobin Ma, Fukun Yan, Can Su, Yi Zhou, Xin Li, Qian Liu, Zijun Hong, Dong Li, Wei Gao, Hua Xu
papers.summary: BiOCl-assisted chemical vapor deposition produces single-crystalline bismuth molybdate nanosheets for high-κ gate dielectrics. Integrated MoS2 transistors retain low hysteresis and useful switching at temperatures up to 500 K. The work addresses dielectric integration and thermal operation in two-dimensional electronics.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Gate-dielectric and interface choices offer relevant device-engineering comparisons for fragile two-dimensional framework crystals.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine material integration challenges in single-crystal electronic devices.

papers.title: Hydroxamate Reticular Chemistry beyond Metals: Single-Crystalline Two- and Three-Dimensional Boron–Hydroxamate Covalent Organic Frameworks
papers.authors: Chaozhi Xiong, Zhiyuan Zhang, Yunxiang Liang, Yihuang Wu, Yitao Tang, Xiaoting Li, Junxing Li, Ziyu Li, Chong Liu
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.archiveJournal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: Hydroxamate chemistry is extended to tetracoordinate boron nodes to construct single-crystalline two- and three-dimensional COFs. Bayesian optimization supports crystal growth, while linker geometry changes framework propagation. Structural and spectroscopic analyses establish mixed bonding, with one framework additionally demonstrating selective carbon-dioxide separation.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Crystallization optimization and topology control offer transferable ideas for designing structurally resolved functional frameworks.

relatedPapers.reason: Both focus on controlling synthesis to obtain well-characterized framework single crystals.

papers.title: A Global-to-Local Diagnostic Scheme Identifies Residual-Defined Local Adsorption Regimes in Metal–Organic Framework Screening
papers.authors: Yu-Juan Yang, Xian-Yang Zhang, Zhi-Wei Qiao, Xue-Ying Yuan, Xue-Qing Gong
papers.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.archiveJournal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.summary: A computational MOF-screening study shows that strong global prediction metrics can hide systematic local adsorption errors. Combining XGBoost with interpretable local models separates broad geometric trends from cavity-chemistry effects across hypothetical frameworks, helping diagnose where screening predictions become unreliable.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Local error analysis could improve how framework structure–property models are interpreted and used to prioritize synthesis.

relatedPapers.reason: Both apply machine learning to framework structure–property relationships and candidate selection.

papers.title: Covalent Organic Framework‐Templated Spatial Confinement of Self‐Assembled Monolayers for High‐Performance Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.authors: Guohao Lang, Junjun Guo, Genping Meng, Zhijie Tang, Du Li, Zhangtao Min, Yuxin Kong, Hengzhe Ma, Ning Li, Xuliang Zhang, Baodui Wang, Jianyu Yuan
papers.versionRelationBasis: Same title, authors and abstract in the English and German Angewandte Chemie editions
papers.summary: A covalent organic framework templates spatially confined self-assembled monolayers at perovskite interfaces. Organized domains suppress aggregation and excessive penetration while improving coverage and subsequent crystallization. The study links framework-mediated molecular assembly to charge extraction and solar-cell performance.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Spatial confinement and interfacial assembly provide synthetic design ideas for controlling ordered molecular layers.

relatedPapers.reason: Both relate molecular organization to the assembly and functional behavior of layered materials.

selectionPolicy: Prefer first discovered in the last 7 calendar days; if a topic has fewer than 3 papers, supplement from days 8–30 to reach 3. Maximum 5 per topic. Never repeat a work.
sourceCoverageNote: All 27 configured rolling feeds were retrieved after retrying four initially unavailable APS feeds. Crossref supplied publication-date metadata for 23 journals. Four dated arXiv API pages returned all 612 records reported at query time. Four supplementary Crossref searches examined the top 30 results each. Candidate-specific arXiv, Crossref and Nature abstract checks supplied reading evidence. A supplementary PMC full-text check required human verification; that paper was reviewed using its publisher-deposited abstract via Crossref. Successful requests and metadata enumeration do not establish exhaustive literature coverage.
